I am 68, and with only two people in the household I will keep this year practical and manageable. I will still plant all four crops, but I will put more land into spring maize because it is the steadiest crop for me under well irrigation and it fits my long farming experience. I will keep some peanut because it sells well and spreads risk, and I will keep smaller areas of cotton and mungbean instead of expanding them, because cotton takes more labor and mungbean needs less fertilizer but usually gives me lower total output. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters for yield and stability, keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate through the well when the crop reaches its key water stages, and do rotary tillage on most land because it is easier for me to manage at my age. I will not run the farm for maximum input; I will run it for dependable yield, lower labor pressure, and lower risk across the season.
